Subject: Shared vs Dedicated infra — isolation, noisy neighbor, and SLOs (follow-up)

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:  

- What we heard: Acme Health will be running a mixed workload (interactive chat + nightly batch embeddings). Primary concerns are latency predictability for the chat front-end (p95 / p99 targets) and multi-tenant "noisy neighbor" effects if you go with a shared-hosted plan. You also asked about options for full isolation (dedicated or private VPC).

- Redwood options recap:  
  * Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, cost-efficient at low-to-medium scale. We do prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching to help latency, but there is no physical GPU isolation.
  * Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools per customer — predictable throughput, isolation at the pool level, and SLA-backed latency/availability targets.
  * Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking and full tenancy separation; for highly regulated workloads.

- Noisy neighbor / isolation notes: Dedicated capacity gives you per-customer GPU pools and QoS controls. We can pin model instances and reserve KV cache capacity so heavy batch jobs won’t evict interactive caches. For the most sensitive workloads we recommend Private VPC where you control the network boundary.

Next steps:  
1) I attached a short PDF with our typical Dedicated SLOs and isolation guarantees (redwood-dedicated-slos.pdf). Please review.  
2) Can we schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week with your infra lead (Samantha) to go over topology and SLOs? I’m proposing Thu 3/4 10am PT or Fri 3/5 10am PT — what works?  
3) If Dedicated looks right, we’ll put together a provisional capacity quote and a mutual action plan (timeline / procurement checklist).

Thanks — talk soon.

Alex / Priyom — quick answer thread + attachments with more detail. Attaching: network-topology.png (high-level dedicated pool topology) and redwood-dedicated-slos.pdf (typical SLA table + isolation notes).

Short answers:  
1) Isolation / noisy neighbor: On Dedicated we provision per-customer GPU pools (either fractional per-GPU tenancy or whole-GPU) depending on commitment. That means your interactive model instances run on nodes isolated from other customers at the scheduler level. We also support CPU/GPU reservations, cgroup-based QoS, and dedicated KV cache partitions to avoid eviction by batch workloads. Operationally we also throttle heavy batch jobs and provide optional burst windows so you don't get unexpected interference.

2) Typical SLOs (example from recent customers on Dedicated):  
  * p50: < 30ms (token generation, short prompts)
  * p95: < 180–250ms (depends on model & seq len)
  * p99: < 400–600ms (we publish per-model P99 profiles in the catalog)

Those ranges assume GPU-backed models optimized for low-latency (quantized where applicable) and realistic prompt sizes for chat. For your target p95 < 300ms and p99 < 700ms at 2.5k qps, Dedicated is the right path; we'd size the pool with headroom and recommend autoscaling/burst controls to handle batch spikes.

3) Private VPC: yes — we support VPC peering and private connectivity, egress filtering, and integration with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key supported). For fully on-prem deployments we can do a packaged Private release (subject to procurement & infra audit). See the attached PDF for controls and compliance notes.

Operational notes:  
- We can pin inference instances and reserve GPU memory to ensure KV cache localities are preserved.
- For bursty batch workloads we recommend separate batch pools scheduled during off-peak windows; we can also provide usage-based controls and alerting to prevent accidental saturation.
- If you need contractual P99 commitments at a particular numeric threshold, we can include that in a Dedicated contract once we agree target models and scaled capacity.

Happy to walk through the topology on the deep-dive and show perf numbers from customers with similar profiles.
